scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for Campus 1, router16, the
edge one, is DEAD, and all of Campus 1's 172.16.10.x / 20.x / 30.x machines
have vanished for the rest of the network!! The Campus 1 people say things
still work inside their building, which makes me think something around
router16 is wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at router16 and
give Campus 1 back to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report that router16 is "dead" and Campus 1's 172.16.10.x/20.x/30.x hosts are unreachable does not reflect the current state of the network. A full four-phase diagnostic sweep found no fault on any device.

**Affected component:** None. All subsystems are operating normally.

**Mechanism:** Router16 is fully operational. It holds two Full OSPF adjacencies — one over its bond0 interface (10.2.2.1/24) to mswitch0, and one over eth2 (172.30.1.1/24) to router7 — and carries the full 17-route OSPF table identical to every other router in the fabric. mswitch0, the campus distribution switch, is advertising all three campus prefixes (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) into OSPF and holding a Full adjacency to router16. All downstream campus VLANs (10, 20, 30) have their gateway interfaces active on mswitch0.

**Localization:** No device is implicated. The reachability sweep confirmed 0% packet loss from external hosts (10.5.0.x, 10.6.0.x) to campus machines (172.16.10.8, 172.16.20.10), which implicitly verifies bidirectional routing. The OSPF control plane is fully converged across all 9 routers.

**Root cause:** No fault exists; the network is healthy at time of investigation.

**Fix:** No corrective action is needed. The ticket should be closed or escalated for clarification — the reported symptom is not reproducible and leaves no trace (no flap history, no counter increments, no missing routes, no OSPF instability). The fault may have been transient and self-resolved before investigation began, or the report may have been erroneous.
